extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners handling priority claims
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for claiming the benefit/right of priority in U.S. and PCT-filed patent applications: what papers to file, time limits, acceptable copies/translations, examiner practice, and remedies for late or missing priority papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to submit priority document (PCT Rule 17.1(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where priority of an earlier national or international application is claimed under Article 8, a certified copy of that earlier application (the “priority document”) shall, unless already filed with the receiving Office together with the international application, be submitted by the applicant to the International Bureau or to the receiving Office not later than 16 months after the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a copy is received by the International Bureau after the expiration of that time limit but before international publication, it shall be considered received on the last day of the time limit. If priority is based on an earlier international application, a copy need not be filed since the International Bureau already has it. If applicant requests early processing under Article 23(2), the priority document must be submitted at that time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office transmittal of priority document (PCT Rule 17.1(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the priority document is issued by the receiving Office, the applicant may request the receiving Office to prepare and transmit the priority document to the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such request must be made not later than 16 months after the priority date and may be subject to payment of a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital-library retrieval alternative (PCT Rule 17.1(bbis))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the priority document is available to the receiving Office or International Bureau from a digital library (per Administrative Instructions), the applicant may request the receiving Office or the International Bureau to obtain and transmit the priority document from that digital library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be made not later than 16 months after the priority date and may be subject to a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of noncompliance with submission obligations (PCT Rule 17.1(c),(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If none of the submission options are complied with, any designated Office may, subject to paragraph (d), disregard the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, a designated Office shall not disregard the priority claim before giving the applicant an opportunity to furnish the priority document within a reasonable time, and shall not disregard it if the earlier application was filed with that Office or is available to it from a digital library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of priority-document copies to designated Offices (PCT Rule 17.2(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant has complied with Rule 17.1, the International Bureau shall, at the specific request of a designated Office, promptly (but not prior to international publication) furnish a copy of the priority document to that Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No designated Office shall ask the applicant to furnish the copy itself. The applicant is not required to furnish a translation to the designated Office before the expiration of the applicable time limit under Article 22. If applicant makes an express request under Article 23(2) prior to publication, the IB shall furnish the copy promptly after receiving it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of priority documents (PCT Rule 17.2(b),(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall not make copies of priority documents available to the public prior to international publication. After publication, copies shall be furnished to any person upon request and cost reimbursement, unless the international application was withdrawn or the relevant priority claim was withdrawn or considered not made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB will withhold public access only until the international application is published; thereafter copies can be obtained subject to cost and exceptions noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim for priority formalities (37 CFR 1.451(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim for priority must be made on the Request (PCT Rule 4.10) in a manner complying with sections 110 and 115 of the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This governs how the priority claim is presented in the international application request form and requires compliance with Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: US Receiving Office-certified-copy request and timing (37 CFR 1.451(b),(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When priority of an earlier U.S. national application or international application filed with the U.S. Receiving Office is claimed, the applicant may request in a letter of transmittal upon filing (or separate letter filed in the USRO not later than 16 months after the priority date) that the USPTO prepare a certified copy for transmittal to the International Bureau; a fee applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the certified copy is not submitted together with the international application or the request/fee is not filed within 16 months, the certified copy must be furnished by the applicant to the International Bureau or U.S. Receiving Office within the PCT Rule 17.1(a) time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required papers for right of priority (35 U.S.C. 119(b) and MPEP §201.14(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: To secure the right of priority, the applicant must (a) file a claim for the right and (b) file a certified copy of the original foreign application (or, for post-AIPA filings, identify the original foreign application by number, authority and date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For original U.S. applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) (other than design) on/after Nov. 29, 2000, the claim must identify the foreign application (application number, country/authority, day, month, year) and any foreign application for same subject matter with an earlier filing date. The claim may be made in the oath/declaration, application data sheet, or transmittal letter; no special form or language is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for presenting claim for foreign priority (37 CFR 1.55(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: In an original application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), the claim for priority must be presented during the pendency of the application and within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application; this time is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: design applications and applications filed before Nov. 29, 2000. For national-stage applications from PCT (after 35 U.S.C. 371 compliance), the claim must be made during pendency and within the time limits set by the PCT/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file certified copy before grant and effects of late filing (37 CFR 1.55(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim for priority and the certified copy of the foreign application must, in any event, be filed before the patent is granted. If filed after the payment of the issue fee it must be accompanied by the processing fee in § 1.17(i), but the patent will not include the priority claim unless corrected by certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and § 1.323.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a post-issue correction is required, a certificate of correction and possibly a grantable petition to accept an unintentionally delayed claim (for post-Nov. 29, 2000 apps) must be filed to have the priority claim considered after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances requiring earlier filing of priority papers (37 CFR 1.55(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require that the claim for priority and the certified copy be filed earlier than the general limits when: (i) the application becomes involved in an interference; (ii) when necessary to overcome the date of a reference relied upon by the examiner; or (iii) when deemed necessary by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases, examiners may set an earlier deadline to ensure prosecution or priority can be properly evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: English translation requirement and timing (37 CFR 1.55(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: An English translation of a non-English foreign application is not required except when the application is involved in an interference, when necessary to overcome the date of a reference relied upon by the examiner, or when specifically required by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a translation is required, it must be filed together with a statement that the translation of the certified copy is accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of untimely claims and petition to accept unintentionally delayed claims (37 CFR 1.55(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any claim for priority not presented within the time period provided is considered waived unless accepted under the provisions of paragraph (c). A late claim may be accepted if the identifying claim was unintentionally delayed and a petition to accept delayed claim is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be accompanied by: (1) the claim for priority (unless previously submitted); (2) the surcharge in § 1.17(t); and (3) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional. The Director may require additional information to determine whether the delay was unintentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner practice in handling priority papers
rubrics_metrics.description: When priority claim and certified copy are received while application is pending, the examiner should make no examination of the papers except to verify that they correspond in number, date and country to the application identified in the oath/declaration and contain no obvious formal defects; the subject matter is not examined for entitlement to the foreign filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For original 111(a) apps filed on/after Nov. 29, 2000, the examiner should also ensure the claim is timely. Use form paragraph 2.21.01 to notify applicant if the foreign priority claim is untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority papers in parent or related applications (continuations/reissues)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a certified copy of the foreign application as filed has been filed in a parent or related application, it is not necessary to file an additional certified copy in the later-filed application; applicant may identify the application containing the certified copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should acknowledge the claim on form PTOL-326. If applicant fails to point out that the certified copy is in the parent, and the examiner is aware of the parent filing, the examiner should call applicant’s attention to this in an Office action so priority data will appear in the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority papers filed in an interference
rubrics_metrics.description: If priority papers are filed in an interference, it is not necessary to file an additional certified copy in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The administrative patent judge will associate them with the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable evidence when original foreign filing was a German model deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: When the only prior 'regular national filing' consisted of a deposit of an actual model (German practice), acceptable evidence of the earlier filing are drawings or clear photographs of the deposited model faithfully reproducing the design, together with required information, certified as a true copy by an official of the court with which the model was deposited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification by the German Patent Office is not necessary; the relevant court's certification suffices. Note AIPA amendment effective Nov. 29, 2000 changed language about certification to refer to 'foreign intellectual property authority.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration identification requirement (37 CFR 1.63)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless provided in an application data sheet, the oath or declaration must identify the foreign application(s) for which priority is claimed and any foreign applications having earlier filing dates by specifying the application number, country (or intellectual property authority), and day, month and year of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification can satisfy part of the statutory/ruled requirements for presenting the priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical recommendation to file priority papers early and label them
rubrics_metrics.description: Because priority papers are sometimes found deficient and there may be insufficient time to remedy defects, it is recommended that priority papers be filed as early as possible and that a pencil notation of the corresponding U.S. application number be placed directly on the priority papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early filing affords time to correct deficiencies (e.g., wrong certified copy) or supply additional documents (a new oath/declaration). Pencil notation helps avoid separation of cover letters and priority papers and eases correlation in the Office.
